decisions.title: Specific-heat units in the solar-heating example
decisions.question: Correct the specific-heat unit to J/(kg·°C), and write the first line as Q/(mc)?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Keep 1670 and the stated 162 °C result; change the unit and make the denominator grouping explicit.
decisions.evidence: Section 11.10, “Solar Electric Generating System,” part (c): the denominator currently contains (0.251 kg)(1670 J·kg/°C). Specific heat must divide by mass for Q/(mc) to have temperature units. The first line Q/mc is also visually ambiguous.

decisions.title: Missing cube in the nuclear-density unit conversion
decisions.question: Cube the entire femtometre-to-metre conversion factor?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. Add an exponent 3 to the whole factor (1 fm / 10⁻¹⁵ m); retain the existing 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³ result.
decisions.evidence: Section 14.4, “How Small and Dense Is a Nucleus?”, part (b): the preceding density is 0.138 u/fm³, but the displayed length-conversion factor has no cube. One power leaves the units incorrect and cannot yield the stated result.
decisions.check: 0.138 × 1.66×10⁻²⁷ × (10¹⁵)³ = 2.2908×10¹⁷ kg/m³, consistent with the existing rounded result.
